[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-004-ai-agent-prompt-governance.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This standard controls prompt quality and change risk in a federated environment. It establishes requirements for canonical prompt structure, prompt versioning, change control tiers, and prompt hygiene — the practices required to prevent prompt sprawl, behavioral drift, and unapproved production forks in a portfolio of AI agents maintained by distributed teams.
page_texts.5:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-004-ai-agent-prompt-governance.md#scope]

### Scope

This standard applies to all prompts, system instructions, and prompt-derived variants used in AI Agents (Configured) and Custom AI Agents at all lifecycle states. It applies regardless of whether prompts are authored in a configuration interface (configured agents) or embedded in code (custom agents).
page_texts.6:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-004-ai-agent-prompt-governance.md#compliance-level]

### Compliance Level

Mandatory. Prompt governance requirements must be in place before any agent is promoted to Pilot state.
page_texts.7:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-004-ai-agent-prompt-governance.md#business-rationale]

### Business Rationale

Prompts are the primary mechanism through which AI agent behavior is defined. In a federated environment where multiple teams can edit, fork, and extend prompts, uncontrolled prompt changes are the most common source of behavioral regressions, policy violations, and quality drift. Canonical prompts and version discipline are the primary controls.

page_texts.9:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-004-ai-agent-prompt-governance.md#mandatory-requirements]

### Mandatory Requirements

**Canonical Prompt Requirements:**

- One canonical prompt per intent — each in-scope intent defined in the capability contract must have exactly one canonical prompt that is the authoritative version
- Canonical prompts must reference the capability contract and output contract — prompts must be authored against the agent's defined output schema and quality requirements
- Cross-cutting policy instructions must be centralized — policy directives that apply across multiple intents (tone, provenance labeling, prohibited content) must be maintained in a shared instruction set and referenced consistently; team-local copies are not permitted
- Local prompt forks are not permitted in Production without architecture board approval

**Versioning Requirements:**

Each prompt version record must include:

1. Version identifier — following the versioning convention in STD-TEC-AI-007
2. Change summary — what was changed in this version
3. Change rationale — why the change was made
4. Impacted intents — which capability contract intents are affected by this prompt version
5. Validation evidence reference — a reference to the test results that validated this version
6. Approval record — the identity and date of the approving authority per the change control tier

**Change Control Requirements:**

| Change Type | Approval Required |
|---|---|
| Minor wording changes (no behavioral impact) | Domain owner approval plus Platform Governance Team validation lead review per STD-GOV-AI-004 |
| Behavioral or output schema changes | Domain owner plus Platform Governance Team review |
| Cross-cutting policy instruction changes | Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board approval |
| Emergency changes (immediate production need) | Expedited approval path; post-change review required within defined window |

For all changes, an emergency rollback path must be documented before the change is released to Production.

**Prompt Hygiene Requirements:**

- Contradictory directives within the same prompt or instruction set are prohibited; prompts must not instruct the agent to do mutually exclusive things
- Redundant variants — near-duplicate prompts with minor wording differences that serve the same intent — must be retired
- Deprecated prompts must be labeled as deprecated and archived; they must not remain in the active prompt library as if current
- Prompt libraries must maintain traceability from each prompt to the active intents it serves; orphaned prompts with no traceable intent must be retired
page_texts.10:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-004-ai-agent-prompt-governance.md#recommended-practices]

### Recommended Practices

- Test prompts against the output contract before promotion to confirm that prompt edits do not inadvertently break required field presence or provenance labeling
- Maintain a prompt library index that maps each prompt to its intent, version history, and validation evidence
- Apply the emergency rollback path for all behavioral changes, not only emergency changes — having a documented rollback path is low cost and high value
page_texts.11:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-004-ai-agent-prompt-governance.md#prohibited-practices]

### Prohibited Practices

- Unapproved local prompt forks in Production state are prohibited
- Prompts that have not passed regression validation may not be promoted to Production
- Deprecated prompts must not be used as the basis for new intent authoring without explicit review
page_texts.12:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-004-ai-agent-prompt-governance.md#exceptions-process]

### Exceptions Process

1. Local prompt fork exceptions require architecture board approval with a documented business justification and a defined sunset date
2. Exceptions to change control tier requirements must be documented with risk assessment and approved by the governance tier that would otherwise have reviewed the change

page_texts.15:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-004-ai-agent-prompt-governance.md#canonical-prompt-storage]

#### Canonical Prompt Storage

- For configured agents: canonical prompts are stored in the agent configuration; the configuration must be under change control per STD-GOV-AI-004
- For custom agents: canonical prompts are stored in version-controlled code or configuration files; changes are governed by the engineering change control process in addition to this standard
page_texts.16:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-004-ai-agent-prompt-governance.md#prompt-version-traceability]

#### Prompt Version Traceability

- Each prompt version record must be stored in a location accessible to the Platform Governance Team for audit purposes
- Version records must not be deleted; deprecated versions are labeled but retained for audit purposes
page_texts.17:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-004-ai-agent-prompt-governance.md#cross-cutting-policy-instruction-centralization]

#### Cross-Cutting Policy Instruction Centralization

- For configured agents: cross-cutting policy instructions are maintained in a shared instruction set that is referenced (not copied) by individual agent configurations
- For custom agents: cross-cutting policy instructions are maintained in a shared prompt module that is imported by agent code; local overrides of shared policy instructions require architecture board approval

---
page_texts.20:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-004-ai-agent-prompt-governance.md#phase-1-canonical-prompt-establishment-before-pilot]

#### Phase 1: Canonical Prompt Establishment (Before Pilot)

1. For each in-scope intent, identify the canonical prompt and store it in the designated prompt library location
2. Confirm that the canonical prompt references the capability contract's output schema and quality requirements
3. Identify any cross-cutting policy directives in the prompt and verify they are sourced from the centralized instruction set
page_texts.21:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-004-ai-agent-prompt-governance.md#phase-2-version-and-change-control-activation-before-pilot-promotion]

#### Phase 2: Version and Change Control Activation (Before Pilot Promotion)

1. Create the initial version record for each canonical prompt with all required fields
2. Document the emergency rollback path for each Production prompt
3. Confirm that the change control tier matrix is understood by all domain contributors
page_texts.22:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-004-ai-agent-prompt-governance.md#phase-3-prompt-hygiene-maintenance]

#### Phase 3: Prompt Hygiene Maintenance

1. Conduct monthly review for prompt drift — prompts that have diverged from their output contract without a version record
2. Identify and retire redundant variants quarterly
3. Label and archive deprecated prompts within one review cycle of their deprecation
page_texts.23:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-004-ai-agent-prompt-governance.md#validation-criteria]

### Validation Criteria

| Validation Area | Criteria | Verification Method | Evidence Required |
| --------------- | --------- | ------------------- | -------------------- |
| One canonical prompt per intent | Exactly one active canonical prompt exists per intent | Prompt library audit | Prompt library index |
| Version records completeness | All active prompts have version records with all required fields | Version record audit | Version record documents |
| Regression validation | All production prompts have passed regression validation | Test results review | Regression validation results |
| Prompt hygiene | No contradictory directives; no redundant variants in active library; deprecated prompts archived | Prompt library review | Prompt hygiene review log |

---
page_texts.25:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-004-ai-agent-prompt-governance.md#non-compliance-handling]

### Non-Compliance Handling

- Unapproved prompt forks in Production: contain the agent and require remediation before restoration
- Missing version metadata on any active prompt: block promotion
- Failed regression validation: rollback to last passing version or contain
page_texts.26:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-004-ai-agent-prompt-governance.md#governance-oversight]

### Governance Oversight

- **Standards Owner**: Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board
- **Compliance Manager**: Platform Governance Team (monthly drift review)
- **Governance Body**: Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board (cross-cutting policy change approval; local fork exceptions)
